newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end little changed amid caution.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end little changed amid caution.

text.p: Argentina's blue-chip Merval stock index closed 0.07 percent higher at 627 on Monday as many investors looked to foreign markets for guidance.
"Little or nothing happened in the market. The fact is the pension funds hardly did anything because they're waiting to see what happens abroad," said Miguel Daneri, an analyst for Boston Security.
Turnover was 15.1 million pesos (15.1 million dollars), down from 18.8 million pesos on Friday.
"There was no decisive demand today to take big positions. There is a lot of caution," Daneri added. He said that volume could pick up again as the week progressed.
The Buenos Aires market was also kept on edge by volatility overseas. Some institutional investors were awaiting the U.S. inflation figures due out Wednesday.
The Banco Crdito Argentino said in a report that the next few days could prove crucial for the local market.
"An even-deeper fall by the Dow .DJI and a rise in long-term interest rates would reduce the possibilities of a continued rise in local stocks," it said.
The Merval lost 1.57 percent Friday, dragged down along with other world markets by remarks by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
Among the best performing stocks on Monday were oil companies Astra and YPF, which rose by 2.45 percent and 2.16 percent, respectively.
